land.text: Pahang, conquered by Malacca in 1454 and governed by Tun Hamzah, then a sultanate under a Malaccan prince

predecessors.note: Infobox: preceded by 'the Malacca Sultanate and the Old Pahang Kingdom'. The pre-1454 kingdom (Ligor's vassal, last ruler Dewa Sura) has no dossier.

land.text: Pahang, in a nominal dynastic union with Johor under Raja Bujang as Abdul Jalil Shah III

successors.note: Infobox: succeeded by the Johor Empire. The page shows Pahang acting independently against Aceh in 1629-1635 and Johor reasserting its authority in 1648, so the union was only nominal; the pahang-sultanate row (1853-1889) is the later Bendahara state.

capitals.name: Pekan
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Pekan'; Matelief arrived at Kuala Pahang in 1607.

correction.text: Pahang, the river basin round Pekan and Kuala Pahang

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria's 'Pahang Sultanate' row is 1853-1889, the later state). The pages give no frontier: the whole of Pahang state (about 36,000 km2) stands for a sultanate on the Pahang river whose capital is Pekan. Infobox area: none.

region.text: Pahang, the river basin round Pekan and Kuala Pahang

ledger.note: c. 1470: Malacca sets up a sultan of its own at Pahang. 'Raja Muhammad was installed as sultan of Pahang as Muhammad Shah, with Tun Hamzah as Bendahara' around 1470; infobox 'Established 1470', 'Vassal state of the Malacca Empire (1470-1511)'. Pahang had been conquered by Tun Perak in 1454 (Dewa Sura taken to Melaka).

region.text: Pekan and its suburbs, the Pahang capital

ledger.note: September 1612: Johor overruns Pekan's suburbs. 'Johor overran Pekan's suburbs in September 1612'.

region.text: Pekan and its suburbs, the Pahang capital

ledger.note: 1613: Pahang defeats Johor with Brunei's help. 'Pahang defeated Johor in 1613 with Brunei's help' (no month on the page).

region.text: Pahang, the river basin round Pekan and Kuala Pahang

ledger.note: 1617: Aceh invades Pahang. Infobox 'Acehnese invasion 1617'; 'Acehnese attacks forced Raja Bujang to flee to Lingga'. The sultanate-of-aceh dossier opens and closes the contest in 1617.

region.text: Pahang, the river basin round Pekan and Kuala Pahang

ledger.note: 1617: the Aceh episode is closed in the year it opens. The page gives no garrison or end date for the Acehnese in Pahang (it has Pahang 'independent' against Aceh in 1629-1635 and Aceh giving up its claim in 1641); the sultanate-of-aceh dossier closes its contest the same year.

region.text: Pahang, the river basin round Pekan and Kuala Pahang

ledger.note: 1623: Pahang enters a union with Johor. 'Pahang entered a nominal dynastic union with Johor in 1623' (infobox '1623 (Personal union with Johor)'); Raja Bujang became ruler of both as Abdul Jalil Shah III. The sultanate-of-johor dossier carries the matching gain.

region.text: Pahang, the river basin round Pekan and Kuala Pahang

ledger.note: 1623: the Pahang Sultanate ends in the union with Johor. The page continues the story of a Pahang that fights Aceh 'independently' in 1629-1635, signs a peace at Bulang Island in 1637 and is attacked by Abdul Jalil III in 1648 'to reassert his authority'.

wars.name: Ligor invasion of Pahang
wars.outcome: 'A Ligor (Nakhon Si Thammarat) army invaded Pahang' in 1500 and was repulsed with Melakan help: the last Siamese invasion.
wars.note: No land changed hands; Pahang's own protector then was Malacca (vassal 1470-1511).

wars.name: Pahang-Johor war of 1612-1613

zones.text: Pekan and its suburbs, the Pahang capital

wars.outcome: Johor overran Pekan's suburbs in September 1612; Pahang defeated Johor in 1613 with Brunei's help.
wars.note: The Johor Sultanate page does not mention this war.

wars.name: Acehnese invasion of Pahang
wars.outcome: Raja Bujang fled to Lingga in 1617; Pahang 'acted independently against Aceh' in 1629-1635, signed a peace treaty at Bulang Island in 1637, and 'Aceh gave up its claim to Pahang' in 1641.
wars.note: The sultanate-of-aceh dossier treats the conquest as a one-year raid.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the whole of Pahang state is a stand-in for the river basin.

sources.title: Johor Sultanate
sources.note: Opened to check the 1623 union and the 1612-1613 war: the page has neither; it has Pahang separate by the 1861 treaty.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for the old sultanate; the 'Pahang Sultanate' row (1853-1889, slug pahang-sultanate, group se-03) shares the same Wikipedia title, which this page tells only of the old state, so the two are different states with one article. This dossier takes the slug old-pahang-sultanate (the one the sultanate-of-malacca dossier already uses as counterpart); the sultanate-of-johor and sultanate-of-aceh dossiers use 'pahang-sultanate' / 'Pahang Sultanate' for the same 1612-1623 events: the reviewer should align the counterpart strings. Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. The Old Pahang Kingdom before 1454 (Ligor's vassal, Dewa Sura) is a separate state without a dossier. The end year (1623) is the infobox's; the page itself shows Pahang acting independently until 1648. Rulers are omitted (the page lists reigns with 'c.' years only).
